prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can I try a crisp sparkling wine from a small producer in Greece? I am curious to taste something new."

List A:
Wine 1: Portuguese Sparkling, Portugal, $34. Tasting note: "This sparkling wine is fresh and crisp. With a creamy texture and a touch of toast, it is very complete and perfumed, with bright acidity to finish. Drink this fragrant wine now."
Wine 2: White Blend, Greece, $22. Tasting note: "A sophisticated, delicate nose of fresh flowers, peach, lemon and spice leads this attractive wine from Greece. On the palate, crisp flavors of lemon, minerals and spice dominate. Refreshing and clean, it will pair well with Asian food, seafood, salads."
Wine 3: White Blend, France, price unknown. Tasting note: "A lightly crisp sparkling wine, given a delicious lift with citrus and mineral components. Floral and fruity, this is fine apéritif wine, just soft enough, an edge of nuts and yeast giving an extra dimension."
Wine 4: Chardonnay, Italy, $29. Tasting note: "Here's a stunning sparkling wine made in the classic method, with no added dosage. It offers citrus, melon, apple, stone fruit, minerality and walnut notes. The creamy palate is supported by crisp freshness and finishes bone-dry."
Wine 5: Portuguese White, Portugal, $11. Tasting note: "Fresh and lightly sparkling, this is a crisp, citrus-driven wine. Its acidity is just right, fruity while well integrated. Some sweetness at the end makes it fine for apéritif drinking."

List B:
Wine 1: Champagne Blend, US, $30. Tasting note: "This pioneering Oregon producer makes a fine, fruity, yeasty sparkling wine from 100% Chardonnay grapes. It’s crisp and lively in the mouth, with medium bubbles and a fresh, citrusy finish."
Wine 2: Sparkling Blend, France, $14. Tasting note: "It makes sense to produce this red sparkling wine in a medium-dry form. That's because the inevitable tannins are modified and are there to give shape to the strawberry fruits and fresh acidity. It's perhaps an acquired taste but would be fine with fruit desserts."
Wine 3: Chenin Blanc, France, $25. Tasting note: "This is a fresh, almond and apple-flavored sparkling wine. With crisp acidity and some attractive bottle aging, it's ripe but cut by a steely aftertaste, and is ready to drink."
Wine 4: White Blend, Italy, price unknown. Tasting note: "Here's a fresh-tasting sparkling wine from northern Italy with pretty aromas of peach, stone fruit and even a touch of melted butter. It has a sophisticated and rich side that is accented by natural sweetness and intense peach flavors."
Wine 5: Chardonnay, France, $25. Tasting note: "Fresh and fruity, this crisp wine comes from a region near Chablis. Good acidity, lively citrus and a cool feel all work well together."
